title: api: schema versioning - deprecations, beta headers, backward-compat shims
description:
Context: We are introducing a V2 request/response schema to support structured output improvements (explicit tool/function calling fields, stable streaming framing, and clearer typing for OpenAI compatibility layer). To avoid breaking existing users we implement a versioning strategy: opt-in beta header, deprecation notices for older fields, and runtime shims that keep legacy clients working for the transition window.

Motivation: Recent regressions in structured output and function-calling edge cases surfaced when consumers upgraded SDKs to rely on the new typed fields. This change bundles the server-side pieces required to: 1) accept X-Redwood-API-Version: 2026-01-beta and route to the new schema; 2) emit deprecation warnings in responses for legacy fields; 3) provide backward-compat shims in the OpenAI compatibility layer to preserve behavior for older SDKs.

What this PR does: 
- Adds a new API schema definition (v2) and a switch in our request middleware to route based on the X-Redwood-API-Version header.
- Introduces runtime shims in pkg/openai/compat that translate v2 typed fields into legacy OpenAI-compatible shapes when needed.
- Emits structured deprecation metadata in the response JSON under a new top-level "deprecations" array for clients to programmatically surface.
- Adds server-side beta header handling and docs for the beta opt-in flow (documentation: docs/api/schema-versioning.md).
- Adds an integration test harness for streaming + function-calling with mixed-version clients and a CI job to exercise the shim paths.

Implementation notes: 
- Header: X-Redwood-API-Version supports values '2025-12' (current default), '2026-01-beta'. When absent we default to legacy behavior to avoid surprises.
- Shims: implemented in pkg/openai/compat/shims.go — they are lightweight translators: v2.structured_output -> choices[].message.content + choices[].message.function_call fields to match historic OpenAI shapes.
- Deprecations: we surface a deprecations array: each entry contains code (string), field (path), message (string), sunset_date (ISO8601). For now entries are informational; we will enforce warnings in logs and the Console UI.
- Rollout: beta header opt-in for 8 weeks, then we plan a staged migration (internal customers, enterprise pilot) before flipping default in a later PR.

Testing and CI: 
- Unit tests for shim translations and header routing. 
- Integration tests simulate a long-lived streaming session where the client upgrades mid-stream; verify no grammar-breaking frames are emitted and the legacy shapes remain available when requested.
- Added a flaky-tolerant rerun for streaming canary tests.

Migration notes for SDKs: 
- SDKs should start honoring the X-Redwood-API-Version header to opt into v2.
- Client authors are encouraged to read docs/api/schema-versioning.md and start switching to typed structured output fields; the compatibility shims will be removed after the sunset_date listed in deprecation entries.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add new schema artifacts and header handling
- [x] Implement compatibility shims
- [x] Add deprecation metadata in responses
- [x] Tests (unit + integration)
- [x] Docs and migration guide

Related: references ENG-4210 (schema-versioning) and ENG-4356 (streaming-stability). See previous background PRs: pr-61234, pr-56321 for earlier header experiments.

review_comments: Marco Ruiz: Overall this looks good. Can you ensure the shims are zero-copy for large streaming payloads? Prefer minimal allocations in shims.go.
Author (Aisha Patel): Updated shims.go to use stream passthrough and only rewrite frames on the fly; added micro-benchmark and notes in shims.go.
Jingwei Zhao: We need a clear sentinel that indicates shimmed responses in logs so on-call can distinguish issues. Suggest adding 'x-rw-shim-applied' debug header.
Author: Added x-rw-shim-applied header when a shim path is executed and added test coverage.
Nora Thompson: Docs LGTM. One minor nit: add an example for mid-stream client upgrade in the migration guide.
release_notes: Introduce v2 API schema behind X-Redwood-API-Version header (2026-01-beta). Adds deprecation metadata and runtime shims to preserve legacy OpenAI-compatible shapes. Beta opt-in for 8 weeks; see docs/api/schema-versioning.md for migration steps.
